name: Maa Kamakhya Temple, Nilachal Hill
path: Maa Kamakhya Temple, Nilachal Hill, Kamrup Metropolitan, India
summary: Foremost of the 51 Shakti Peethas on Nilachal hill, celebrating feminine procreative power and Ambubachi Mela.
points: Original shrine built during Mlechchha dynasty; present hybrid Nilachal-style beehive shikhara temple rebuilt in 1565 CE by King Nara Narayana of the Koch dynasty
Sanctum holds no anthropomorphic image but a natural stone fissure fed by an underground natural spring
Celebrates the annual Ambubachi Mela in June marking the annual menstrual cycle of Mother Earth

name: Kaziranga National Park
summary: UNESCO World Heritage sanctuary protecting over 2,600 great Indian one-horned rhinoceroses.
points: Established as a reserve forest in 1905 by Mary Curzon; declared UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985
Protects the world's largest population of great one-horned rhinoceroses and wild water buffaloes
Spans 430 sq km of alluvial floodplains, dense elephant grass, and marshes along the Brahmaputra River
